questions.stem: What does the woman say she really appreciates?
questions.stemZh: 女士说她真正欣赏的是什么?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: W: But I really appreciate all the details that go into the game. 女：但我真的很欣赏这款游戏里所有用心做出来的细节。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 态度信号词 really appreciate。女方亲口说 I really appreciate all the details that go into the game，really appreciate 是直白的『看重』信号，紧跟其后的 all the details 就 是她真正欣赏的对象；这种态度词后紧接的宾语正是细节题的答案落点。

analysis.text: all the details that go into the game ↔The details in the driving simulator. details 原词 + game=simulator 同指

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 Traveling all over the country. 蹭了男方 parts of the country you don't normally see 里的 country，但那是男方谈被风景吸引时说的，且女方 appreciate 的是 details，不是 『走遍全国』，对象与人都对不上。 借用原文：parts of the country you don't normally see B) 原词陷阱 Driving from one city to another. 几乎照抄女方 driving from one city to another 的原 词，但女方说这句是在描述游戏内容『就是把货从 A 运到 B』，紧接着才说她真正欣赏的是 details——这句是铺垫，不是 appreciate 的对象。 借用原文：driving from one city to another D) 偷换概念 The key role of the logistics industry. 借了女方 a new appreciation for the logistics industry 的原词，但那是她欣赏 details 后『额外』生出的一个感受，且 a new appreciation 是顺带提及，本题问的 really appreciate 直接指向 details。 借用原文：a new appreciation for the logistics industry

questions.stem: What outcome does the woman expect from the driving simulator?
questions.stemZh: 女士期望从驾驶模拟器中获得什么结果?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: W: But if it results in more drivers looking both ways before entering an intersection, I'd say that's a positive outcome. 女：但如果它能让更多司机在进入路口前左右观望（更小心），我会说那是个积极的结果。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 假设 + 积极评价的期望句。女方在末段用 if it results in more drivers looking both ways…I'd say that's a positive outcome，if…I'd say that's a positive outcome 是典型 的『假设带来的好结果』语气，正是 expect 的对象所在；这种带 if / positive outcome 的 句子是结果题的定位信号。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: more drivers looking both ways before entering an intersection ↔More people driving safely. 具体行为概括为安全驾驶 that's a positive outcome ↔More people driving safely. positive outcome 印证这是她期待的结果

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 Clearer road signs. 蹭了男方 obeyed all the road signs and traffic rules 里的 road signs，但那是男方描述直播玩家守规矩时说的，女方期待的是『人更小心驾驶』，不是 『路标更清晰』，人和内容都不对。 借用原文：obeyed all the road signs and traffic rules C) 原词陷阱 Stricter traffic rules. 借了男方 obeyed all the road signs and traffic rules 里的 traffic rules，但录音从没说要『更严的交规』，更没出自女方的期望句，纯属拿原词改造出的无中 生有。 借用原文：obeyed all the road signs and traffic rules D) 答非所问 More self-driving trucks on the road. 直接搬了女方 self-driving trucks may soon be available 的原词，但女方说自动驾驶卡车是在『分析行业前景』时提的客观可能，不是她 对模拟器期待的 outcome；本题问的期待结果落在末段那句安全驾驶上。 借用原文：self-driving trucks may soon be available 1 W: How do you like being self-employed? W: 你觉得自己当老板怎么样？ 2 M: There are obvious benefits, though I don't seem to have the freedom I anticipated as I just don't seem able to decline work offers. And working alone, there have been times when I've found that money alone provides insufficient motivation. Have you experienced the same since you began working for yourself? M: 有明显的好处，不过我似乎没有预期的那种自由，因为我就是没法拒绝工作机会。而且独自工作的时 候，有时候我发现光靠钱提供不了足够的动力。你自己开始为自己工作以后也有同样的感受吗？ 3 W: Sometimes, yes. Unlike the rest of the workforce who have managers to prompt motivation whenever they're feeling lazy or bored, we self-employed workers perform our jobs without a manager to lift our spirits. There's no one around to offer praise or initiate collaboration, no one to make greater use of our interests and talents. W: 有时候是这样。不像其他有经理在懒散或无聊时激励他们的劳动者，我们这些自雇工作者做工作时没 有经理来提振精神。周围没有人给予表扬或发起合作，没有人更好地利用我们的兴趣和才能。 4 M: That's a fact. Not every manager behaves with such awareness and care, of course. And certainly not all managers have a clue how to motivate people. Still, having a manager nearby at least indicates Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard. there's an opportunity they'll be decent enough to look out for you when your energy and focus begin to deplete. M: 这是事实。当然，不是每个经理都有这样的意识和关怀。而且肯定不是所有经理都知道怎么激励人。 不过，至少有个经理在身边意味着有机会他们会足够体面，在你精力和注意力开始消耗的时候照顾你。 5 W: The motivator I value most is autonomy. I've learned not to sacrifice my prized autonomy by working all hours of the day and by saying yes to every client request. W: 我最看重的激励因素是自主权。我已经学会不通过整天工作、对每个客户要求都说好来牺牲我珍视的 自主权。 6 M: Yes. I need to remind myself that I selected this lifestyle for the independence. I don't miss aspects of permanent full-time employment I disliked, such as the office politics, job insecurity, inflexible hours and so on. I wouldn't mind a bit more in the form of praise though, praise which is on the record. M: 是的。我需要提醒自己，我选择这种生活方式就是为了独立。我不怀念全职固定工作中我不喜欢的那 些方面，比如办公室政治、工作不安全感、不灵活的工作时间等等。不过我倒是不介意多一点表扬，那种 有记录的表扬。 7 W: That'll come with time. Relatedness is inevitably cultivated via human interaction. Engaging with clients, getting written testimony and recommendations, staying in contact with clients afterwards, these are things you'll find will come in due course and provide you with motivation. W: 那会随着时间到来的。人际关系必然是通过人际互动培养的。与客户接触、获得书面证言和推荐、事 后与客户保持联系，这些事情你会发现会在适当的时候到来，并给你提供动力。 8 M: You're right. That's an area I do need to put some more effort into—building closer relationships with those who engage my services and skills. M: 你说得对。这是我确实需要多下功夫的一个方面——与那些使用我的服务和技能的人建立更紧密的 关系。

questions.stem: What does the man say about managers?

questions.answerText: Not all of them know how to motivate their employees.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Not every manager behaves with such awareness and care, of course. And certainly not all managers have a clue how to motivate people. 当然，并非每位经理都那么有觉察、有关怀。而且，确实并非所有经理都懂得如何激励 员工。

analysis.text: 范围词 not every／not all 直接定调。男士连用 Not every manager behaves with such awareness and care 和 not all managers have a clue how to motivate people，两 个"not every/not all"是部分否定，明确说"并非全部"，这正是范围题的答案信号。

analysis.text: A) 偷换概念 录音说 Not every manager behaves with such awareness and care，讲的是"并非每位 经理都有觉察与关怀"，而非 Not all of them care about their employees' behaviors."不 在意员工的行为"——care 的对象被偷换：原文是经理自己有没有 care，选项变成"在不在 意员工的 behaviors"。 借用原文：Not every manager behaves with such awareness and care B) 与原文相反 选项 Few of them are aware of their employees' feelings. 用 Few（几乎没有）替换了 原文的 not all（并非全部），范围被大幅夸大；且 awareness 原文修饰的是经理的觉察， 不是专门"察觉员工 feelings"。 借用原文：Not every manager behaves with such awareness and care C) 张冠李戴 Few of them offer praise and reward to their employees. 里的 praise 来自女士那句 There's no one around to offer praise，谈的是"自雇者身边没人给表扬"，并非男士对"经 理群体"的概括，且又把范围说成 Few，张冠李戴又改范围。 借用原文：There's no one around to offer praise

analysis.label: 定位

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 表态词 You're right 后承接的观点。男士开口 You're right 明确表示赞同，紧接着复述他 认同的那件事 building closer relationships with those who engage my services and skills，表态词后承接的内容就是"他同意的那一点"。

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 张冠李戴 The need for getting recommendations from their managers. 里的 recommendations 来自女士第7段 getting written testimony and recommendations， 但那是从客户处获取，选项偷改成"从经理处获取"，而自雇者根本没有经理，张冠李戴。 借用原文：getting written testimony and recommendations C) 与原文相反 录音里 permanent full-time employment 出现在男士 I don't miss aspects of permanent full-time employment I disliked，他说的是"不怀念全职的那些方面"，与"全 职的优点"恰恰相反，The advantages of permanent full-time employment. 反了向。 借用原文：I don't miss aspects of permanent full-time employment I disliked D) 张冠李戴 The way to explore employees' interests and talents. 里的 interests and talents 来自 女士第3段 no one to make greater use of our interests and talents，谈的是自雇者没人 来发掘自己的兴趣才能，并非男士"赞同"的那一点，张冠李戴又偏题。 借用原文：no one to make greater use of our interests and talents Section B 1 Weather is a constant force in our lives, but there is little marketing research on how it affects businesses. Now, a new study reveals how sunny and snowy conditions influence consumer behavior. 天气是我们生活中的一个恒定力量,但关于天气如何影响企业的营销研究却很少。现在,一项新研究揭示了 晴朗和下雪的天气条件如何影响消费者行为。 2 Those weather conditions trigger consumers to mentally visualize using products associated with the respective weather. This leads to consumers placing a higher value on those products. That is, they're willing to pay more money for them. But the correlation is only found with products related to being outside. 这些天气条件会触发消费者在心理上想象使用与相应天气相关的产品。这导致消费者对这些产品赋予更高 的价值。也就是说,他们愿意为这些产品支付更多的钱。但这种相关性只存在于与户外相关的产品中。 3 How does this work? Researchers give the example of a beach towel. On a sunny day, consumers who see that product are not just looking at the towel itself, they are likely imagining themselves lying on the towel in the sun. Studies conducted in the 1970s and 1990s suggested that people felt less happy when alone as compared to being with others. It had a couple of shortcomings. First, it measured emotion on a scale from positive to negative, overlooking the possibility that our positive and negative emotions can fluctuate independently. Also, it categorized emotions as simply positive or negative. It didn't consider that emotions arouse us to different degrees, and that both positive and negative emotions can arouse us a lot or a little. That is, whether positive or negative, emotions can be either high-arousal or low-arousal. High-arousal emotions include excitement on the positive side or anger on the negative side, while low-arousal ones include feeling calm on the positive side or lonely on the negative. 让我们先来看看早期的研究。它存在几个缺陷。首先,它在从积极到消极的量表上测量情绪,忽略了我们的 积极情绪和消极情绪可以独立波动的可能性。此外,它将情绪简单地归类为积极或消极。它没有考虑到情绪 以不同程度唤醒我们,并且积极和消极情绪都可以在很大或很小程度上唤醒我们。也就是说,无论是积极还 是消极,情绪都可以是高唤醒或低唤醒的。高唤醒情绪包括积极方面的兴奋或消极方面的愤怒,而低唤醒情 绪包括积极方面的平静或消极方面的孤独。 Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard. 3 This new research attempted to overcome these shortcomings. Researchers began with a simple study. They asked participants to spend 15 minutes sitting alone without engaging in any activity, and measured how this solitude influences their emotional state. This experiment specifically aimed to determine the effect of solitude on high-arousal emotions. It looked at positive emotions such as being excited or interested, and negative emotions including being scared or distressed. The results were clear. After 15 minutes of solitude, the participants showed reductions in both types of emotion. 这项新研究试图克服这些缺陷。研究人员从一项简单的研究开始。他们要求参与者独自坐15分钟而不参与 任何活动,并测量这种独处如何影响他们的情绪状态。该实验特别旨在确定独处对高唤醒情绪的影响。它考 察了积极情绪,如兴奋或感兴趣,以及消极情绪,包括害怕或痛苦。结果很明确。在独处15分钟后,参与者表现 出这两种类型情绪的减少。 4 A second study measured the effects of solitude on low-arousal emotions. These included both positive and negative emotions, such as feeling calm, relaxed, sad or lonely. That experiment found that all of these emotions were increased by time alone. Thus it seems past depictions of solitude were wrong. It doesn't have a simple emotional effect that can be characterized as good or bad. Rather, it changes the intensity of our inner experience. It amplifies quieter emotions, but it diminishes the intensity of stronger feelings. 第二项研究测量了独处对低唤醒情绪的影响。这些情绪包括积极和消极情绪,如感到平静、放松、悲伤或孤 独。该实验发现,所有这些情绪都因独处时间而增加。因此,过去对独处的描述似乎是错误的。它没有可以 被描述为好或坏的简单情绪效应。相反,它改变了我们内心体验的强度。它放大了较平静的情绪,但减弱了 较强烈感受的强度。 5 It's worth clarifying that these findings relate to relatively brief periods of solitude. This is distinct from prolonged loneliness. Research has demonstrated that the latter is correlated with an assortment of negative physical and psychological effects. How can people benefit from being alone? The findings here suggest that people can use solitude to regulate their emotions. Solitude can help us become quiet after excitement, calm after an angry episode, or simply feel at peace. 值得澄清的是,这些发现与相对短暂的独处时期有关。这不同于长期孤独。研究表明,后者与一系列负面的 生理和心理影响相关。人们如何从独处中受益?这里的发现表明,人们可以利用独处来调节他们的情绪。独 处可以帮助我们在兴奋后变得安静,在愤怒发作后平静下来,或者只是感到平和。

Does that mean that thinking harder is a simple route to losing weight? 1984年,世界国际象棋锦标赛突然被叫停,原因是一名争夺冠军头衔的棋手身体极度消瘦。他并非唯一一个 经历这种极端身体反应的人。据报道,精英棋手一天可以燃烧高达惊人的6000卡路里。这是否意味着更努 力地思考是减肥的简单途径? Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard. 2 Well, when the body is at rest, we know that the brain uses up a startling 20% to 25% of the body's overall energy. This level of utilization actually makes the brain the most energy-expensive organ in the body, and yet it makes up only 2% of the body's weight overall. 我们知道,当身体处于静息状态时,大脑消耗的能量占身体总能量的惊人的20%到25%。这种利用水平实际 上使大脑成为身体中能量消耗最昂贵的器官,然而它仅占身体总重量的2%。 3 So the more we put this organ to work, the more calories we'll burn? Technically, the answer is yes, for cognitively difficult tasks. What counts as a "difficult" mental task varies between individuals. But generally, it could be described as something that the brain cannot solve easily using previously learned routines, or tasks that change the conditions continuously. 那么我们越多地使用这个器官,就会燃烧越多的卡路里吗?从技术上讲,对于认知困难的任务,答案是肯定的。 什么算作"困难"的心理任务因人而异。但通常可以描述为大脑无法使用先前学习的常规轻松解决的事情,或 者不断改变条件的任务。 4 However, deep thinking will not burn off the calories gained from eating a sugary snack. Because in relation to the brain's huge overall energy usage, which is devoted to a multitude of tasks, the energy required just to think harder is actually comparatively tiny. A lot of that activity is unrelated to conscious activities like learning how to sing or play the guitar. 然而,深度思考不会消耗掉吃一份含糖零食所获得的卡路里。因为相对于大脑巨大的总体能量使用(用于多 种任务),仅仅为了更努力思考所需的能量实际上相对微小。我们意识不到大脑能量消耗的大部分活动。这 些活动中有很多与学习唱歌或弹吉他等有意识的活动无关。 5 The brain is able to allocate blood (and thus energy) to particular regions that are being active at that point. analysis.label: 拆句

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: The reason, of course, is that on some level they don't want a solution; they want to be validated in their position that the world is out to get them. If they can "win" the game— dismissing every suggestion until their interlocutor gives up in annoyance—they get to feel pleasurably righteous in their resentments and excused from any obligation to change. 原因当然是，在某种程度上他们并不想要解决方案；他们想要的是自己"世界与我作对"的立 场被认可。如果他们能"赢"——通过驳回每一个建议直到对话者厌烦放弃——他们就能在怨 恨中感到正当的快感，并被免除任何改变的责任。

A) Our world is full of—mostly untold—stories of slow hope, driven by the idea that change is possible. They are 'slow' in their unfolding, and they are slow because they come with setbacks.
B) At the beginning of time—so goes the myth—humans suffered, shivering in the cold and dark until the titan(巨人) Prometheus stole fire from the gods. Just as in the myth, technology—first fire and stone tools, and later farming, the steam engine and industry, fossil fuels, chemicals and nuclear power—has allowed us to alter and control the natural world. The myth also reminds us that these advances have come at a price: as a punishment for Prometheus' crime, the gods created Pandora, and they gave her a box filled with evils and curses. When Pandora's box was opened, it unleashed swarms of diseases and disasters upon humankind.
C) Today we can no longer ignore the ecological curses that we have released in our search for warmth and comfort. In engineering and exploiting and transforming our habitat, we have opened tens of thousands of Pandora's boxes. In recent decades, environmental threats have expanded beyond regional boundaries to have global reach and, most hauntingly, are multiplying at a dizzying rate. On a regular basis, we are reminded that we are running out of time. Year after year, faster and faster, consumption outpaces the biological capacity of our planet. Stories of accelerated catastrophe multiply. We fear the breakdown of the electric grid, the end of non-renewable resources, the expansion of deserts, the loss of islands, and the pollution of our air and water.
D) Acceleration is the signature of our time. Populations and economic activity grew slowly for much of human history. For thousands of years and well into early modern times, world economies saw no growth at all, but from around the mid-19th century and again, in particular, since the mid-20th, the real GDP has increased at an enormous speed, and so has human consumption. In the Middle Ages, households in Central Europe might have owned fewer than 30 objects on average; in 1900, this number had increased to 400, and in 2020 to 15,000. The acceleration of human production, consumption and travel has changed the animate and inanimate spheres. It has echoed through natural processes on which humans depend. Species extinction, deforestation, damming of rivers, occurrence of floods, the depletion of ozone, the degradation of ocean systems and many other areas are all experiencing acceleration. If represented graphically, the curve for all these changes looks rather like that well-known hockey stick: with little change over millennia(数千年) and a dramatic upswing over the past decades.
E) Some of today's narratives about the future seem to suggest that we too, like Prometheus, will be saved by a new Hercules, a divine engineer, someone who will mastermind, manoeuvre and manipulate our planet. They suggest that geoengineering, cold fusion or faster-than-light spaceships might transcend once and for all the terrestrial constraints of rising temperatures, lack of energy, scarcity of food, lack of space, mountains of waste, polluted water—you name it.
F) Yet, if we envisage our salvation to come from a deus ex machina(解围之神), from a divine engineer or a tech solutionist who will miraculously conjure up a new source of energy or another cure-all with revolutionary potency, we might be looking in the wrong place. The fact that we now imagine our planet as a whole does not mean that the 'rescue' of our planet will come with one big global stroke of genius and technology. It will more likely come by many small acts. Global heating and environmental degradation are not technological problems. They are highly political issues that are informed by powerful interests. Moreover, if history is a guide, then we can assume that any major transformations will once again be followed by a huge set of unintended consequences. So what do we do?
G) This much is clear: we need to find ways that help us flatten the hockey-stick curves that reflect our ever-faster pace of ecological destruction and social acceleration. If we acknowledge that human manipulation of the Earth has been a destructive force, we can also imagine that human endeavours can help us build a less destructive world in the centuries to come. We might keep making mistakes. But we will also keep learning from our mistakes.
H) To counter the fears of disaster, we need to identify stories, visions and actions that work quietly towards a more hopeful future. Instead of one big narrative, a story of unexpected rescue by a larger- than-life hero, we need multiple stories: we need stories, not only of what Rob Nixon of Princeton University has called the 'slow violence' of environmental degradation (that is, the damage that is often invisible at first and develops slowly and gradually), but also stories of what I call 'slow hope'.
I) We need an acknowledgement of our present ecological plight but also a language of positive change, visions of a better future. In The Principle of Hope (1954-1959), Ernst Bloch, one of the leading philosophers of the future, wrote that 'the most tragic form of loss…is the loss of the capacity to imagine that things could be different'. We need to identify visions and paths that will help us imagine a different, more just and more ecological world. Hope, for Bloch, has its starting point in fear, in uncertainty, and in crisis: it is a creative force that goes hand in hand with utopian(乌托邦的) 'wishful images'. It can be found in cultural products of the past—in fairy tales, in fiction, in architecture, in music, in the movies—in products of the human mind that contain 'the outlines of a better world'. What makes us 'authentic' as humans are visions of our 'potential'. In other words: living in hope makes us human.
J) The power of small, grassroots movements to make changes that spread beyond their place of origin can be seen with the Slow Food movement, which began in Italy in the 1980s. The rise of fast-food restaurants after the Second World War produced a society full of cheap, industrially made foodstuffs. Under the leadership of Carlo Petrini, the Slow Food movement began in Piedmont, a region of Italy with a long history of poverty, violence and resistance to oppression. The movement transformed it into a region hospitable to traditional food cultures—based on native plants and breeds of animals. Today, Slow Food operates in more than 160 countries, poor and rich. It has given rise to thousands of projects around the globe, representing democratic politics, food sovereignty, biodiversity and sustainable agriculture.
K) The unscrupulous( 无所顾忌的) commodification of food and the destruction of foodstuffs will continue to devastate soils, livelihoods and ecologies. Slow Food cannot undo the irresistible developments of the global food economy, but it can upset its theorists, it can 'speak differently', and it can allow people and their local food traditions and environments to flourish. Even in the United States—the fast-food nation—small farms and urban gardens are on the rise. The US Department of Agriculture provides an Urban Agriculture Toolkit and, according to a recent report, American millennials(千禧一代) are changing their diets. In 2017, 6 per cent of US consumers claimed to be strictly vegetarian, up from 1 per cent in 2014. As more people realise that 'eating is an agricultural act', as the US poet and environmental activist Wendell Berry put it in 1989, slow hope advances. 36. It seems some people today dream that a cutting-edge new technology might save them from the present ecological disaster.

P1 Vegetarians would prefer not to be compelled to eat meat. Yet the reverse compulsion(强迫) is hidden in the proposals for a new plant-based "planetary diet." Nowhere is this more visible than in India.

P2 Earlier this year, the EAT-Lancet Commission released its global report on nutrition and called for a global shift to a more plant-based diet and for "substantially reducing consumption of animal source foods." In countries like India, that call could become a tool to aggravate an already tense political situation and stress already undernourished populations.

P3 The EAT report presumes that "traditional diets" in countries like India include little red meat, which might be consumed only on special occasions or as minor ingredients in mixed dishes. Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.

P4 In India, however, there is a vast difference between what people would wish to consume and what they have to consume because of innumerable barriers around class, religion, culture, cost, geography, etc. Policymakers in India have traditionally pushed for a cereal-heavy "vegetarian diet" on a meat-eating population as a way of providing the cheapest sources of food.

P5 Currently, under an aggressive Hindu nationalist government, Muslims, Christians, disadvantaged classes and indigenous communities are being compelled to give up their traditional foods.

P6 None of these concerns seem to have been appreciated by the EAT-Lancet Commission's representative, Brent Loken, who said "India has got such a great example" in sourcing protein from plants.

P7 But how much of a model for the world is India's vegetarianism? In the Global Hunger Index 2019, the country ranks 102nd out of 117. Data from the National Family Health Survey indicate that only 10 percent of infants of 6 to 23 months are adequately fed.

P8 Which is why calls for a plant-based diet modeled on India risk offering another whip with which to beat already vulnerable communities in developing countries.

P9 A diet directed at the affluent West fails to recognize that in low-income countries undernourished children are known to benefit from the consumption of milk and other animal source foods, improving cognitive functions, while reducing the prevalence of nutritional deficiencies as well as mortality.

P10 EAT-Lancet claimed its intention was to "spark conversations" among all Indian stakeholders. Yet vocal critics of the food processing industry and food fortification strategies have been left out of the debate. But the most conspicuous omission may well be the absence of India's farmers.

P11 The government, however, seems to have given the report a thumbs-up. Rather than addressing chronic hunger and malnutrition through an improved access to wholesome and nutrient-dense foods, the government is opening the door for company-dependent solutions, ignoring the environmental and economic cost, which will destroy local food systems. It's a model full of danger for future generations.

reading-2.raw:
P1 Back in 1964, in his book Games People Play, psychiatrist Eric Berne described a pattern of conversation he called "Why Don't You—Yes But", which remains one of the most irritating aspects of everyday social life. The person adopting the strategy is usually a chronic complainer. Something is terrible about their relationship, job, or other situation, and they moan about it ceaselessly, but find some excuse to dismiss any solution that's proposed. The reason, of course, is that on some level they don't want a solution; they want to be validated in their position that the world is out to get them. If they can "win" the game—dismissing every suggestion until their interlocutor(对话者) gives up in annoyance— they get to feel pleasurably righteous(正当的) in their resentments and excused from any obligation to change.

P2 Part of the trouble here is the so-called responsibility/fault fallacy(谬误). When you're feeling hard done by—taken for granted by your partner, say, or obliged to work for a half-witted boss—it's easy to become attached to the position that it's not your job to address the matter, and that doing so Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage. would be an admission of fault. But there's a confusion here. For example, if I were to discover a newborn at my front door, it wouldn't be my fault, but it most certainly would be my responsibility. There would be choices to make, and no possibility of avoiding them, since trying to ignore the matter would be a choice. The point is that what goes for the baby on the doorstep is true in all cases: even if the other person is 100% in the wrong, there's nothing to be gained, long-term, from using this as a justification to evade responsibility.

P3 Should you find yourself on the receiving end of this kind of complaining, there's an ingenious way to shut it down—which is to agree with it, ardently. Psychotherapist Lori Gottlieb describes this as "over-validation". For one thing, you'll be spared further moaning, since the other person's motivation was to confirm her beliefs, and now you're confirming them. But for another, as Gottlieb notes, people confronted with over-validation often hear their complaints afresh and start arguing back. The notion that they're utterly powerless suddenly seems unrealistic—not to mention rather annoying—so they're prompted instead to generate ideas about how they might change things.

P4 "And then, sometimes, something magical might happen," Gottlieb writes. The other person "might realise she's not as trapped as you are saying she is, or as she feels." Which illustrates the irony of the responsibility/fault fallacy: evading responsibility feels comfortable, but turns out to be a prison; whereas assuming responsibility feels unpleasant, but ends up being freeing. 51. What is characteristic of a chronic complainer, according to psychiatrist Eric Berne? A) They only feel angry about their ill treatment and resent whoever tries to help. B) They are chronically unhappy and ceaselessly find fault with people around them. C) They constantly dismiss others' proposals while taking no responsibility for tackling the problem. D) They lack the knowledge and basic skills required for successful conversations with their interlocutors.

writing.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay on why students should be encouraged to effective communication skills. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
writing.model: Effective communication is far more than a soft skill; it is a core competence that shapes a student's academic success and professional future. For this reason, schools and teachers should actively encourage students to develop this valuable ability from an early stage. There are several compelling reasons for this. First, strong communication skills facilitate learning. When students can clearly express doubts and exchange ideas in group projects, knowledge is absorbed far more efficiently. Moreover, these skills sharpen employability. In job interviews, an applicant who articulates thoughts logically leaves a stronger impression than one who merely lists qualifications. In addition, good communication enriches personal relationships, helping students voice their emotions and resolve conflicts with empathy. Such emotional connection is essential for a healthy campus life. In conclusion, effective communication benefits students in study, career and daily life alike. Schools should therefore create more opportunities—debates, presentations and teamwork—so that every student can grow into a confident and articulate communicator.

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 桥作主语，串两个表语（主语策略：原句主语） 中文主语明确就是「大桥」，对应 港珠澳大桥(Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge)全长55公 里。可把主谓宾定为 The Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge is an extraordinary engineering feat（主语 The bridge ＋ 系动词 is ＋ 表语 feat），把「全长55公里」当成主语的修饰信息先放 一边。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 「全长55公里」降级成定语 「全长55公里」不必单独成句，可处理成同位语 a 55-kilometer-long sea crossing 或后置定语 with a total length of 55 kilometers 挂到主干上，对应 全长55公里；「我国一项」译成 in China / China’s 即可，无须把「我国」拗成独立分句。整句重构为 The Hong Kong-Zhuhai- Macau Bridge, with a total length of 55 kilometers, is an extraordinary engineering feat in China.

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 回指全篇基调，用一般现在时 is——陈述这座桥现在就是一项工程壮举。 冠词 feat 是可数单数、表「一项」，前面要加不定冠词 an（an extraordinary…，注意 extraordinary 读音以元音开头用 an）。 复合形容词单复数 作前置定语的 55-kilometer-long 里 kilometer 用单数（连字符复合形容词中名词不加 s）；若用 with a total length of 55 kilometers 作后置，则 kilometers 用复数。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: The Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge, with a total length of 55 kilometers, is an extraordinary engineering feat in China. 2. 大桥将三个城市连接起来，是世界上最长的跨海桥梁和隧道系统。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 桥作主语，两个动作取一为主干（主语策略：原句主语） 主语仍是大桥，对应 大桥将三个城市连接起来。中文有「连接」「是…系统」两个谓语，可取「是 世界上最长的…系统」作主干 It is the longest sea-crossing bridge-and-tunnel system in the world，把「连接三个城市」降级处理。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 「连接三城」降级成现在分词定语 把「将三个城市连接起来」改写成现在分词短语 connecting the three cities 作后置定语或伴随状 语，挂到主干上，对应 大桥将三个城市连接起来：It is the longest sea-crossing bridge-and- tunnel system in the world, connecting the three cities. 避免写成 The bridge connects… and is… 的双谓语流水句。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 用一般现在时 is／connecting，回指全篇基调，陈述客观事实。 最高级冠词 「最长的」用最高级 the longest，最高级前必须加定冠词 the。 单复数 「三个城市」是复数，译 the three cities，cities 加 s；特指这三座具体城市，用定冠词 the。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: It is the longest sea-crossing bridge-and-tunnel system in the world, connecting the three cities. 3. 大桥将三个城市之间的旅行时间从3小时缩短到30分钟。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 桥作主语，缩短作谓语（主语策略：原句主语） 主语仍是大桥（用 It 承接），核心动词是「缩短」，宾语是「旅行时间」，对应 大桥将三个城市 之间的旅行时间从3小时缩短到30分钟。主干定为 It cuts the travel time… from… to…。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 「从…到…」降级成 from…to… 状语 「从3小时缩短到30分钟」用 from three hours to 30 minutes 作状语挂在动词后，对应 从3小时 缩短到30分钟；「三个城市之间的」用介词短语 between the three cities 作 travel time 的后置 定语：It cuts the travel time between the three cities from three hours to 30 minutes.

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 用一般现在时 cuts／reduces，陈述这座桥现在就具备的功效；主语 It 单数第三人称，谓语加 s。 主谓一致 主语 It 是第三人称单数，动词须用 cuts／reduces（带 s），这是主体考生最易漏的三单。 用词搭配 「缩短（时间）」用 cut／reduce／shorten 均可，搭配 time 自然；数字 3 小时可写 three hours（小数字宜用英文单词），30 分钟写 30 minutes，复数加 s。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: It cuts the travel time between the three cities from three hours to 30 minutes. 4. 这座跨度巨大的钢筋混凝土大桥充分证明中国有能力建造创纪录的巨型建筑。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 桥作主语，证明作谓语带宾语从句（主语策略：原句主语） 主语是「这座…大桥」，核心动词「证明」，宾语是「中国有能力建造…」这一整件事，对应 充分 证明中国有能力建造创纪录的巨型建筑。主干定为 This… bridge fully proves that China is capable of…，宾语用 that 从句承载。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 「跨度巨大的钢筋混凝土」作前置定语，「有能力做」用 be capable of doing 「跨度巨大的」「钢筋混凝土」都作 bridge 的前置定语：This massive reinforced concrete bridge，对应 这座跨度巨大的钢筋混凝土大桥；「有能力建造」用 be capable of building 或 has the ability to build，「创纪录的巨型建筑」译 record-breaking mega-structures 作宾语。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 主句 proves 用一般现在时（回指基调）；that 从句 is capable 也用现在时，陈述当下事实。 介词搭配 be capable of 后接动名词 building（of＋doing），不可接动词原形；若改用 the ability to build 则接动词原形。 单复数 「巨型建筑」泛指一类、非特指某一座，用复数 mega-structures／giant structures，不加 the。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: This massive reinforced concrete bridge fully proves that China is capable of building record-breaking mega-structures. 5. 它将助推区域一体化，促进经济增长。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 它作主语，两个动作并列（主语策略：原句主语） 主语「它」承上指大桥，用 It；「助推」「促进」是两个并列动作，宾语分别是「区域一体化」 「经济增长」，对应 它将助推区域一体化，促进经济增长。主干 It will boost… and promote…， 两动词共用主语、用 and 并列。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 本句结构简单，两宾语用固定搭配译出即可 无需深度降级。「区域一体化」译 regional integration，「经济增长」译 economic growth，对 应 助推区域一体化，促进经济增长，两个动宾用 and 连成 boost regional integration and promote economic growth 即可。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 中文「将」表对未来的推动作用，用一般将来时 will boost… and promote…（这是允许偏离现在 时基调的一处：明确指向未来效应）。 并列动词形式一致 and 连接的两个动词须同形：will boost 后省略 will，接动词原形 promote（will boost… and promote…），不可写成 promotes。 单复数与冠词 integration、growth 均为不可数抽象名词，不加冠词、不加复数。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: It will boost regional integration and promote economic growth. 6. 大桥是中国发展自己的大湾区总体规划的关键。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 桥作主语，是…关键作主干（主语策略：原句主语） 主语是大桥（用 The bridge 或 It），核心是判断句「是…的关键」，对应 大桥是中国发展自己的 大湾区总体规划的关键。主干 The bridge is key to…／is the key to…。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 「中国发展自己的大湾区总体规划」整体作 to 的宾语 把「中国发展自己的大湾区的总体规划」处理成名词短语 China’s master plan to develop its own Greater Bay Area，作 key to 的宾语，对应 中国发展自己的大湾区总体规划；「发展…」用 不定式 to develop 作 plan 的后置定语。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 用一般现在时 is，回指基调，陈述当下事实。 搭配与冠词 be key to 中 key 作形容词时可不加冠词（is key to）；若 key 作名词则用 the key to。to 是介 词，后接名词短语 China’s master plan，不接动词。 物主代词 「自己的」译 its own——指代中国（国家用 its），呼应主语 China，别误用 his／their。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: The bridge is key to China’s master plan to develop its own Greater Bay Area. 7. 中国希望将大湾区建成在技术创新和经济繁荣上能与旧金山、纽约和东京的湾区相媲美的 地区。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 中国作主语，希望作谓语带不定式（主语策略：原句主语） 主语是中国，核心动词「希望」，对应 中国希望将大湾区建成…地区。主干 China hopes to turn the Greater Bay Area into a region…，用 hope to do＋turn… into… 搭骨架，后面那一大串 「能与…相媲美的」是修饰 region 的定语，留到下一步降级。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 「能与…相媲美的」降级成定语从句 把「在技术创新和经济繁荣上能与旧金山、纽约和东京的湾区相媲美的」改写成定语从句 that rivals／can rival the bay areas of San Francisco, New York and Tokyo in technological innovation and economic prosperity，修饰 a region，对应 在技术创新和经济繁荣上能与旧金 山、纽约和东京的湾区相媲美的地区；「在…上」用介词 in 引出比较的方面。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 China hopes 用一般现在时（回指基调，陈述中国当前的愿望）；定语从句 rivals／can rival 也用 现在时。 主谓一致 主语 China 第三人称单数，谓语 hopes 加 s；定语从句先行词是单数 a region，关系代词 that 作 主语时动词用 rivals（加 s）。 并列名词与介词 「旧金山、纽约和东京」三个并列专名 San Francisco, New York and Tokyo，最后两项间用 and；「在…方面」用 in（in technological innovation and economic prosperity），别误用 on。 用词 「相媲美」用 rival／be comparable to／match；「技术创新」technological innovation， 「经济繁荣」economic prosperity，均为抽象不可数名词，不加冠词。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: China hopes to turn the Greater Bay Area into a region that rivals the bay areas of San Francisco, New York and Tokyo in technological innovation and economic prosperity. 英语六级 2020年12月·第2套 · 全卷构成 Part III Part III Part III Part III
